assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks reaching the 10^-18 fractional-uncertainty regime are a direct realisation of the idea that progress is set by what can be measured and how accurately. The magic-wavelength lattice concept removes Doppler and recoil shifts, and the resulting clocks now enable tests of fundamental constants, relativistic geodesy and a path to a redefinition of the second. Clear, original and of lasting impact, and squarely in the tradition of spectroscopy and frequency-metrology prizes.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength optical lattice scheme and realised the first strontium lattice clock; Ye's group drove the systematic-uncertainty and coherence record-setting, including the many-body (Fermi-degenerate) clock. A two-person prize is natural and fair; other contributors (for example Ludlow, Hinkley, Derevianko, Takamoto) are not credited in the supplied names and the broader clock community overlaps with the 2005 and 2012 prizes.
assessment.maturity: Independent confirmation across several laboratories (JILA, RIKEN, NIST, PTB, SYRTE and others) and 10^-18 comparisons are well established. Timely, with the redefinition of the second under discussion; arguably not premature.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2005 frequency-comb and 2012 prize themes could be seen as incremental by some colleagues.
Allocation between lattice-clock concept and precision-record achievement is not fully separable; I rely on memory for details of priority.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realise the Hubbard model with tunable parameters, with the superfluid to Mott insulator transition, single-site-resolved quantum gas microscopes and Fermi-Hubbard studies. The field built a new tool for many-body physics and quantum simulation, and is influential across atomic physics and condensed matter. Original, clear and enduring.
assessment.attribution: Zoller (with Jaksch, Cirac and colleagues) supplied the theoretical proposal and the framework; Greiner and Bloch carried out the Mott transition and microscope work; Esslinger led the fermionic Hubbard realisation and Cirac is a theory co-author. The five credited names exceed three slots, so a hard choice is required and the one chosen leaves out Esslinger and Cirac; Jaksch, who co-authored the key proposal, is not credited.
assessment.maturity: Mature: two decades of replication by many groups and quantitative benchmarking of simulators. Timely and not premature, though the biggest simulation-scale payoffs remain ahead.
uncertainties: Credit allocation among five named people and uncredited theorists (such as Jaksch) is genuinely contested.
Zoller overlaps with other AMO candidates on the list; the committee might treat quantum-simulation and quantum-computing strands together.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Atom interferometry turned matter-wave coherence into a precision instrument, with applications to measurements of gravity, rotation, the fine-structure constant and tests of the equivalence principle. It is a flagship demonstration of quantum sensing with individual quantum particles, and I regard it as important though its eventual impact on fundamental questions is still developing.
assessment.attribution: Pritchard produced early atom interferometers and the first demonstrations with a Mach-Zehnder-type geometry; Bordé gave the theoretical framework (Ramsey-Bordé interferometer, relativistic phase shifts); Kasevich developed the light-pulse gravimeters and gradiometers with record sensitivity. Chu (already awarded in 1997) and Schmiedmayer (atom chips and matter-wave interferometry) are important to the story and Schmiedmayer is in the supplied list; four-name credit forces an exclusion.
assessment.maturity: Established across several groups and growing commercial and space missions; maturity is good but headline fundamental-physics results (e.g., a new bound or discovery) are still limited.
uncertainties: Several equally deserving contributors compete for three places.
Fundamental discovery content, as opposed to technique, is weaker than for the clock candidate.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Realising strongly interacting Fermi gases and tuning through the BEC-BCS crossover via Feshbach resonances established a clean, controllable system for strongly correlated fermionic superfluidity, relevant for neutron stars, high-Tc physics and universality. The scientific clarity and ability to compare with quantitative theory are impressive.
assessment.attribution: Early observations by Thomas (strongly interacting degenerate Fermi gas), Grimm (molecular BEC and crossover, collective modes), Salomon (also Jin, Ketterle, Zwierlein, Hulet). Deborah Jin, a pivotal contributor, died in 2016 and cannot share, which complicates a fair allocation. Ketterle already holds the 2001 prize for BEC.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed by many groups for almost two decades; maturity is clear, though the case can look like a natural continuation of the BEC prize.
uncertainties: Credit allocation is complicated by the death of a key contributor and by many parallel groups.
Possible perception as a follow-on to the 2001 prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical detection and coherent control of single nitrogen-vacancy centres in diamond opened solid-state quantum sensing with nanoscale resolution under ambient conditions, including magnetometry and spin-based biological sensing. A clear, original and widely used platform, closely related to my own field of coherent optical addressing of spins in crystals.
assessment.attribution: Wrachtrup and Jelezko made the first single-NV optical detection and coherent control; Lukin contributed major sensing and quantum-register developments, with others (Hanson, Awschalom, Walsworth, Budker, Yacoby) also central. Because of my own interest in coherent light-matter interactions in doped crystals, I recognise a potential perceived proximity, though I have no documented direct relationship to these candidates.
assessment.maturity: Replicated widely and used in applications; the discovery stage is mature, while many sensing applications are still emerging.
uncertainties: Overlap with the separate B010 candidate (optical spin interfaces) means a prize could be framed in different ways.
Contributions from other groups may be understated in the three-name credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit quantum electrodynamics created a controllable platform for light-matter interaction at the quantum level with superconducting artificial atoms, and underpins the leading superconducting quantum processors and readout schemes. High impact for quantum information and quantum optics.
assessment.attribution: Blais, Huang, Wallraff, Girvin and Schoelkopf published the 2004 proposal and the first strong-coupling demonstration; Girvin is credited in the supplied list but excluded here for the three-name limit. Allocation between theory (Blais, Girvin) and experiment (Wallraff, Schoelkopf) is delicate and not resolved from the supplied text alone.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed and mature as a technique; however the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits is recent, which suggests waiting before another superconducting-circuit award.
uncertainties: Timing relative to the recent superconducting-circuit prize.
Four credited names must be reduced to three.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theoretical prediction of flat bands at magic angles and the discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene created the field of moiré quantum matter and twistronics, with very rapid and broad impact on condensed matter.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the magic angle; Jarillo-Herrero's group experimentally discovered correlated insulating states and superconductivity. Credit seems well-defined as a theory plus experiment pairing, though others, for example Dean (hBN heterostructures), Yacoby and later groups, also contributed.
assessment.maturity: Replicated widely since 2018, but the physical mechanism of the superconductivity is still debated, and the field is young, so recognition is arguably somewhat early.
uncertainties: Timing may be premature compared with more mature candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Detection of a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos and the establishment of neutrino astronomy with IceCube, including the association with blazar TXS 0506+056 and the galactic-plane map, is a remarkable measurement achievement opening a new window on the universe. Importance is high even if outside my own field.
assessment.attribution: Halzen is the single supplied name and was a primary scientific leader of the IceCube concept; the discovery was a very large collaboration effort, and one-person recognition would leave a fair-credit question (other founding scientists and the collaboration leadership). I cannot judge fine details of who was decisive.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by observations accumulating since 2013 with independent analyses; the source identification is still partly open, making the case solid but evolving.
uncertainties: Source identification remains incomplete, and I am not an expert in astroparticle physics.
